newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says birth control ruins people's moral sense.
newsitem.headline: Pope says birth control ruins people's moral sense.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Saturday artificial birth control was ruining people's moral sense by giving a false idea of sexual freedom.
He attacked "unbridled hedonism" which was slowly creating an "eclipse of values".
The Roman Catholic Church considers artificial birth control and abortion a sin.

The Pope said in a letter to the head of the Vatican's Institute of Bioethics: "Worrisome consquences have been produced in the sexual sphere of life by a false sense of freedom provided by contraception, which is both an incentive and a tool."
"This has brought about a softening of people's consciences and an eclipse of values," the Pontiff said in his letter to Bishop Elio Sgreccia.
He criticised public health campaigns that promote contraception as a "duty" to society.
The Pope said "an unbridled hedonism and a disdain for life" was at the heart of the modern world's moral quandary.
"The 'Gospel of Life' must be maintained by educating children to recognise their vocation as carriers of life, in responsible collaboration with...the creator," he said.
